title: 2D Contour with level link keep_down: generation takes minutes, almost all of it in verify_bodies

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported timing on a plate with about 8.5k facets and inside rings (entry helix, helix
angle 4, level keep_down):

| rings | time |
|---|---|
| 1 | 4 s |
| 2 | 7.6 s |
| 4 | 20 s |
| 8 | 70 s |

That is about n^1.5. `max_stay_down` does not help.

Finding. All timings are from a debug build (local repro, 43,268 facets, 1/8 in tool, entry helix, helix angle 4,
`level: keep_down`, `transition: ramp`, inside rings picked on the plate):

| rings | moves | kernel `contour()` | `verify_bodies` | `generate` total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 541 | 1.7 s | 29.3 s | 31.1 s |
| 2 | 2,173 | 2.3 s | 115.2 s | 117.7 s |
| 4 | 4,909 | 3.9 s | not isolated | 378 s |
| 8 | 9,865 | 6.1 s | not isolated | 1,018 s |

Without keep_down: 65, 150, 305 and 630 moves; 5.6, 8.9, 21.5 and 54.2 s.

- The kernel is not the cause: 6 s for 8 rings.
- About 94 percent of the time is `verify_bodies` in `generate.rs`. It costs about 54 ms for each
  move with 43k facets, with or without keep_down. The cost is linear in the move count.
- Keep_down posts 8 to 15 times more moves for the same rings (the ramp legs), so it is
  8 to 15 times slower. A slower growth than linear in the rings comes from the larger rings.
- `solid_hits` already has a `SolidIndex`. The slow sub-step inside `verify_bodies` is not isolated.
  It needs a profiler inside `verify_bodies`.

Needed: find the slow step in `verify_bodies` for a long ramped path, or cut the move count of a
keep-down ramp. A STEP model with 4 to 14 mm through holes reproduces it (not attached here).

Proposed labels (a collaborator sets them): bug, source:agent, P3, effort:high, area:2d
